clock_dir_minute_5: Russian genitive cardinal minute count in the subtractive "без N <hour>"
clock idiom -- generalises the fixed quarter idiom ("без четверти девять")
to any minute count: "без пяти девять" == without five == 08:55.  Bound
only after CLOCKDIR ("без"); it is not a toward-hour bare-fraction word
(unlike FRACTION's "четверть"/"половина", it names no bare "N of the
hour" idiom on its own -- "пять девять" alone is not Russian for a clock
time), so it lives in its own map rather than clock_fractions.
clock_dir_to: Russian subtractive clock: "без четверти десять" == without-a-quarter ten ==
09:45 -- "без" subtracts the fraction from the NAMED (reached) hour.
clock_fraction_15: Russian toward-hour clock: "четверть десятого" == a quarter OF the tenth ==
09:15 (bare_quarter_to).  The genitive "четверти" is the subtractive form,
"без четверти десять" == a quarter TO ten == 09:45 (CLOCKDIR "без").
clock_fraction_30: Russian toward-hour clock: the half NAMES the coming hour with a genitive
the ninth == 08:30.  Handled by the bare_half_to + toward_hour_12h
conventions.  Citation: gramota.ru (Russian State Language reference
service), telling the time -- "половина <genitive ordinal>" counts toward
the coming hour.  The locative "половине" is the same half after the clock
preposition "в": "Приходите в половине двенадцатого" (Pushkin, quoted in
В. И. Максимов, "Половина первого, полпервого?", 1973, p. 53).

ночь as "часть суток между вечером и утром (примерно от полночи до 6
часов)" (https://ru.wiktionary.org/wiki/ночь), which names no clock hour

afternoon1 [12:00, 18:00)), so "15:30 ночи" names no time.

marker_ad: The secular "нашей эры" / "н. э." and the religious "по Р. Х." (по

Справочник издателя и автора, §7.1.6 gives "29 авг. 284 г. н. э." as the
model, and Викисловарь records "по Р. Х." as its Christian equivalent
marker_alarm_at: The noun of a clock that sounds at a set time, and "на" after it: "будильник
на семь".  "будильник [...] часы, подающие звуковой сигнал в заданное время",
example "Он ставит будильник мобильного телефона на 7:30" (Wiktionary, s.v.
"будильник").  Alice voice commands give the same shape: "Поставь будильник
на 8 утра по будням", "Переведи будильник на 10 утра"
marker_bc: Russian dates the pre-Christian past with the secular "до нашей эры",
abbreviated "до н. э." with a space after each letter; that spaced form is
the norm set by Мильчин and Чельцова, Справочник издателя и автора, §7.1.6
The unspaced "до н.э." is what people type in practice, so it is read too.
The religious counterpart "до Р. Х." (до Рождества Христова) is equally
current and means the same span of years.

falls in.  The HOURSPAN order of clock_time reads it.

marker_last: Russian "last/previous" determiner, the full adjectival paradigm.  The
temporal phrase almost never stands in the nominative: "на прошлой неделе"
takes the prepositional, "в прошлом месяце" and "в прошлом году" take the
prepositional masculine/neuter, and "прошлым летом" takes the instrumental.
Shipping only the nominative would leave the ordinary spoken register
unreadable, so the whole hard-stem adjective paradigm (Грамота.ру,
"Склонение прилагательных": твёрдая разновидность, тип "новый") is listed.
marker_minut: Russian optional "минут" (genitive plural "minutes") that may follow the
minute count in the subtractive clock idiom: "без пяти минут девять" ==
"без пяти девять" == 08:55.  Citation: gramota.ru, telling the time.
marker_month_word: The noun "месяц" in the genitive after a day: "пятого числа прошлого
месяца" names the fifth day of the previous month.  Bound only after
"<ordinal> числа REL_MARKER", where the marker names the month outright.
Source: Wiktionary, s.v. месяц, sense 1, "период времени — двенадцатая
in the same entry, genitive singular "месяца".
marker_na: The preposition the week phrases take: Russian frames a relative week with
"на" and the prepositional case, where the month and year take "в".
CLDR 47 gives "на прошлой неделе", "на этой неделе", "на следующей неделе"
marker_next: Russian "next/following" determiner, the full adjectival paradigm.  As with
"прошлый" the temporal phrase is normally oblique -- "на следующей неделе",
"в следующем месяце", "в следующем году" -- so the soft-stem paradigm
is listed in full rather than the citation form alone.
